events.author: Velociryx
events.name: A Display of Benevolence

options.text: I will not risk angering my vassals. Conquering our enemies can wait. Let's keep the peace at home.
My vassals can choke on their desire for benevolence. We're fighting this war to its logical conclusion!

events.text: You war against [rival] is going well. Perhaps too well. Having crushed a good portion of their forces, a groundswell movement has begun from the ranks of your vassal families, with an increasing number of people, some in high positions in your Court, calling on you to demonstrate your benevolence and declare an end to the fighting. Total victory is within your grasp, but in order to achieve it, you'll need to weather some storms at home. What say you?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: A Solemn Procession

options.text: May [religion] unite our people.
Call an end to the war and invite one of the visiting to the court.
Devoted followers of [religion] are always welcome in [city], but the war is a separate matter.
[rival] ways have corrupted [religion]. We want nothing to do with either.

events.text: A solemn procession of [religion] arrives from [rival] at the holy city of [city]. The are watched closely by the city guard as they pass through the gates. As in [rival], [religion] holds great sway on [rival] rule, and the nature of the visit is political rather than spiritual. [character] requests that we set aside our differences in the name of our shared faith. How shall you respond?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Balancing Act

options.text: Keeping my vassals happy is more important than continuing the fight. We shall heed their advice and make a truce with [rival]... for now.
[character] forgets his place. I am the ruler of these lands. The fighting stops when I say it does.
Put [character] in prison for his insolence and let us speak no more about the matter.

events.text: Your war against [rival] is progressing splendidly. Unfortunately, there are a growing number of people in your vassal families who have grown war-weary and wish to see hostilities end. The loudest voice calling for a truce is [character], who is gaining increasing support for his position at Court. How will you respond?

events.author: Solver
events.name: Bloodshed Among the Righteous

options.text: For the sake of all our people, let the fighting stop.
The war is a tragedy, but the needs of [rival] demand it.
[rival] does not interpret the holy books as you do. They are not true [religion].

events.text: [character] requests an audience to inform you that many of his fellow [religion] believers are pained by our war with [rival]. Whatever earthly conflicts we may have, the war means righteous blood is shed. [religion] priests have considerable say in [rival] palace affairs, and can ensure a truce is accepted if we are willing to stop the fighting.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Bonds of Faith

options.text: By all means. Our people's hearts are weary. If shared faith between our leaders can forge a truce, let it be so.
Since our envoys were sent, we have had a change of heart. Our war will continue.

events.text: Having accomplished our major goals in our war with [rival], our envoys carried an offer of truce to them on the basis of a shared bond of faith between us and [character]. [rival] is willing to call an end to hostilities on the basis of that bond, but the final decision is ours to make.

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Cultural Similarities

options.text: Fortune smiles! Let us call an end to hostilities at once!
The situation has changed since we dispatched our emissaries. Although the road ahead is fraught with peril, a truce no longer serves our interests.

events.text: two nations have artisanal traditions in common and we were able to leverage these to get them to the truce table.

events.text: two nations have a shared love of knowledge, and our sages have been working quietly behind the scenes to end the conflict. They have succeeded, against all odds.

events.text: two nations have a number of talented statesmen who have been working quietly behind the scenes to bring the war to a close. Those efforts have finally been successful.

events.text: two nations both have influential merchant vassal families, and they want peace desperately. Fortunately, their arguments have prevailed.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Day of the Darkened Sun

options.text: Make an offer of peace to [rival].

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Refuse to let your actions be guided by the gods.

requirements.label: Cunning / Schemer
tip: The leader must have one of: Cunning; Schemer

options.text: Bribe the priests to claim that the omens are on your side.

events.text: The war with [rival] is stretching on without any sign of ending. After a day where the sun is darkened in the sky, [character] claims that the omens all show that and the gods disapprove of the ongoing war. Is this a sign to make peace?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Familial Ties

options.text: Perfect! Let us cease hostilities at once!
[character] did a great thing in securing us a truce offer, but conditions have changed. We simply can’t take it.

events.text: Our war with [rival] has been a tremendous success, but having weakened them, we dispatched [character], who shares a blood tie with them, in hopes of ending hostilities. Those efforts have succeeded! All that remains now is for us to formally accept a truce with [rival].

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Family Traditions

options.text: Excellent! We shall cease hostilities at once!
The situation has changed since we dispatched our emissaries. A truce no longer serves our interests.

events.text: based on the close ties and commonalities shared by the Artisan Guilds that our Artisan families share in common.

events.text: based on the shared honor code that our Champions families share in common.

events.text: based on philosophies and doctrine that our Clerical families share in common.

events.text: brokered by the most capable statesmen we have, who are communicating quietly with members of their counterparts in [rival].

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Foreign Rule

options.text: [character] will not dictate [rival] rule!
Very well. I will do it for [character].
We will instead invite a member of the [rival] nobility to join our court.
[character] is a fool, but surely this envoy can teach us things we don’t yet know.

events.text: The suffering inflicted upon [rival] at the hands of the [rival] has taken its toll on your husband, [character]. His shared heritage with the enemy has left him in a unique state of torment that you wish you could better understand, let alone abate. Just as you realize that all known paths to peace have grown over in your idleness, a serendipitous envoy arrives from [rival]. “I bring word from [character]. He has not forgotten that his compatriot shares your bed and sits by your throne. His grace is willing to call an end to the war,” the envoy pauses a moment. “On the sole condition that [rival] take over rule.”

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Heaven Help Us

options.text: Consider this a gift from the heavens and let us cease hostilities and begin to rebuild.
Although our envoys did a great thing, our hearts have changed on the matter. Our war must continue.

events.text: Our war with [rival] does not go well. Fortunately, the riders we recently sent out to sue for peace have just returned and report that they have found success, appealing to the fact that both we and [character] share the same faith. There is a glimmer of hope for us. [character] shares our faith and beseeches us to see reason and end this bloodshed, agreeing to live peacefully as brothers and sisters of the faith. This could be a lifeline. We need but take it.

events.author: Josh Unsworth
events.name: Kneel and Obey

options.text: Kneel and accept.
Refuse to surrender.

events.text: The [rival] diplomats are accompanied by an entourage of serious, resplendent in their fine robes. The diplomats explain that [character] is willing to end the war if [rival] adopts [religion] as your State Religion. Will you surrender your god for the sake of peace?

events.author: Velociryx
events.name: Lucky Break

options.text: We shall be eternally grateful for the efforts of [character]. Let there be an end to the hostilities.
[character] did a wonderfully brave thing, but conditions have changed since he undertook the effort. We must continue the war to the best of our abilities.

events.text: The war with [rival] has been calamitous, and as we have sought a way out, [character] approached us and offered to leverage his relations with [rival] to bring about the end of the war between our peoples. Those efforts appear to have borne fruit. We need but accept it.

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Pause in Hostilities

options.text: Yes, let us unite against a common foe.
No, we do not want to provoke the [tribe].

events.text: Our enemies, the [rival], are willing to declare a truce if we will join their war against the [tribe].

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: Shared Histories

options.text: Alas, peace is not the best path forward for [rival].
Very well. Let us end this war.
You are right, [character]. Please accept this gift of good will, and let our nations move forward together.
You should not have come here, [character].

events.text: Whispers cut through the court as a procession of [rival] arrives outside the capital gates. Surrounded by his personal guard, [character] himself has come to the capital to discuss a possible truce between our nations. You take the proper precautions before giving audience to the [rival] [title]. After some discussion of practical matters, [character] appeals to your shared traditions. “Although we are at war, the ways of [rival] and [rival] are not so different. Our people follow similar customs and are ruled by many of the same laws: [law], [law], and [law], to name a few. Perhaps it is time we set aside our differences and focus on our shared histories.”

events.author: Andy Auseon
events.name: Stop the Fighting

options.text: [character] is right, we must make a truce.
Appoint him head of a war council.
Convince [character] of the conflict's necessity.

events.text: With a storm of fiery rhetoric, [character] condemns our ongoing War with [rival], claiming that you are personally profiting from the deaths of our soldiers. He demands an immediate cessation of hostilities and a formal review of our military conduct. How shall we respond?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Keen Edge of War

options.text: Yes. Let’s focus on the greater threat.
We have no qualms with [rival].
There are more subtle ways to deal with [rival].
Guards, arrest this trespasser.

events.text: As skirmishes with [rival] continue, both sides shy away from the keen edge of war. After a night of heavy rains, the dawn brings with it a travel-weary messenger from [city]. Caked with mud and on the brink of exhaustion, the courier, whose emblem you recognize as belonging to one of the noble families of [rival], takes a moment to focus before reading a message from [character]. “While our two great nations squabble, [rival] grows ever more powerful. We must set aside our differences and focus our joint might on [rival], before it is too late and we are all speaking.” How will you respond to [character]’s offer?

events.author: Brodie Frehlich
events.name: The Problem at Hand

options.text: No. I see right through [rival]’s excuses.
Yes, let’s shift our focus to the [event].
Perhaps our nations can work through this problem together.

events.text: In light of the recent [event], [rival] has sent an envoy to the capital to request a temporary Truce. [character] feels that it would be in both our nations’ best interests to focus on domestic affairs at this time. Will you agree to a Truce?

events.author: Leyla Johnson
events.name: Time for a Truce

options.text: We will return the hostage to end the war.
We are not ready to stop the fight.

events.text: An unassuming envoy from [rival] enters the court, head bowed courteously. He states that he has been given authority to speak for his nation's leadership. The [rival] will gladly establish a truce and end the fighting, if only we will return their hostage.

events.author: Soren Johnson
events.name: Time for a Truce

options.text: Let us end this.
Not yet!

events.text: A group of riders approaches our front lines, led by an envoy from [character]. In respectful terms, he extends an offer of truce. [rival] is willing to end the fighting.

events.name: Worthy Opponents

options.text: Agreed! Let us put an end to the fighting for now.
No.

events.text: The [rival] sent us a truce parley. Respectful of the military skills we demonstrated, they suggest that our people need not shed any more blood to prove their valor on the field. They came with gifts as a sign of benevolence and respect.
